careerDirection.directionDescription: Entrepreneurship is a career path where the graduate chooses to create and run their own venture rather than work as an employee. Using the knowledge, skills, and domain expertise built through their degree, the graduate identifies an opportunity and builds a business around it — whether a local enterprise, a freelance practice, a professional service, a digital venture, or a scalable startup. The graduate is the owner, the decision-maker, and the driver of the work.

careerDirection.directionDescription: Academic and research careers in AI involve contributing to scientific advances in machine learning, deep learning, and AI safety. Research associates support faculty research projects; research fellows work on funded research programmes; AI research analysts work in industry research labs. BCA AI & ML graduates who pursue higher education (MTech, MSc, or PhD) can enter academic research careers — at BCA level, research associate, online tutor, and EdTech content creator roles are the realistic entry points into the research-adjacent track.

careerDirection.directionDescription: Cloud infrastructure for AI involves managing the compute, storage, and networking resources that train and serve ML models. Cloud engineers provision GPU instances for training; platform engineers build ML infrastructure platforms; DevOps engineers automate model deployment workflows. BCA AI & ML graduates who add cloud platform certification alongside their ML training are competitive for these infrastructure-adjacent roles that support large-scale AI deployments.
